title: CLAIM: Organized satanic cults abused children en masse in the 1980s
summary: Dozens of daycare ritual-abuse prosecutions collapsed nationwide (McMartin: zero convictions; Keller convictions overturned, declared actually innocent 2017). The FBI's 1992 Lanning report found no evidence of large-scale organized satanic cults. Nearly all the accused were eventually freed.
tldr: The single Wikisource page reviewed (p. 20 of the FBI's 1992 Lanning report) describes how investigators approached 'multidimensional child sex rings' — it is not the report's conclusion section.
ai_summary:
AI review of Wikisource page 20 of the FBI's 1992 'Investigator's Guide to Allegations of Ritual Child Abuse' (Kenneth Lanning), read in full:
- Discusses the 'bizarre or ritualistic activity' dynamic: victims reporting ceremonies, chanting, robes, drugs, animal sacrifice, torture, abduction, murder — with Lanning's caution that 'bizarre' may be a better word than 'ritual' for the activity.
- Introduces his term 'multidimensional child sex rings' for multioffender/multivictim cases; notes as many as 40–50% of reported offenders in these cases are women, contrasting with historical child sex rings where almost all offenders are men.
- Notes the trend of victims evaluated by 'experts' trained to specialize in satanic ritual abuse whose prior experience with these dynamics was 'none.'
- Discrepancy flag: this is one page of the report, not its conclusion — it contains no statement about the absence of large-scale organized satanic cults and no mention of McMartin or the Keller case. The record summary's claims (Lanning's no-evidence conclusion; McMartin zero convictions; Keller convictions overturned and 2017 actual-innocence declaration) could not be verified from this page. Verification against the named primary source is therefore incomplete.
